title: Writing and ordering rules: deny by default

videos.script: A developer installs a cache on a server and tells nobody. Under one kind of firewall, the whole internet can reach it the moment it starts. Under the other kind, nobody can. {{cache}} This lesson is about that choice, deny by default, and about the habits that keep a rule set safe to change. {{deny}} You will break a rule file with one misspelt word, and see that nothing half-applies. {{atomic}} You will lock yourself out on purpose, with a way back already scheduled. And you will watch the way back itself go wrong, in a way worth knowing before a real night. {{rollback}} Then the firewall's own door, why ICMP is not optional, and a log of what the policy drops. {{log}}
